subject.title: [Bug]: Non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text '[tool: exec]' instead of tool_use blocks

question: How should OpenClaw handle a non-native provider response that contains only a bare tool marker such as `[tool: exec]` with no arguments or structured tool call?
rationale: Executing a synthesized tool call is unsafe without arguments, while retry, fallback, blocking, or warning behavior all change provider/runtime compatibility policy.

options.title: Fallback or block safely
options.body: Detect the bare marker as failed tool intent, avoid executing fabricated arguments, and fall back or warn/block when a tool-capable model is required.

options.title: Retry same provider
options.body: Retry once with stronger tool-call instructions or forced tool choice, accepting that weak providers may repeat the stall.

options.title: Document as unsupported
options.body: Keep promoting only complete serialized calls and document that bare markers from incompatible providers are not recoverable.

recommendation.title: Fallback or block safely
recommendation.body: Detect the bare marker as failed tool intent, avoid executing fabricated arguments, and fall back or warn/block when a tool-capable model is required.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent provider-stream policy and runtime refactor history makes this the best available owner for the product-direction choice.
